title: AI-Based Medication Intake Monitoring – Perspectives and Challenges in Adherence Management (Module A)
summary:
The regular and correct intake of medication is essential for older adults or individuals with chronic conditions to avoid health complications and prevent the progression of diseases. However, there are numerous challenges that make the medication intake difficult, including forgetfulness, comprehension issues, or uncertainties in handling medications. As a result, a significant number of affected individuals do not take their medication as prescribed. Digital technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), offer the potential for support – such as personalized reminders, motivational communication, or automated intake monitoring.

In this study, interviews are conducted to explore the experiences, challenges, and concerns older adults or feriatric patients face regarding medication intake and the use of digital technologies. Additionally, this study aims to determine the specific requirements that an AI-based application would need to meet in order to improve the daily lives of those affected.
To broaden these perspectives, an additional interview will be conducted with a respective relative, as well as focus group discussions which will involve healthcare professionals. The findings are intended to develop digital support solutions that not only improve long-term medication adherence among older adults but also contribute to enhancing overall healthcare delivery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria for individual interviews with older adults or geriatric patients: 
• Fully consenting, community-dwelling older adults (≥ 65 years) OR geriatric patients in outpatient, partial inpatient, or inpatient care (≥ 65 years)
• Currently taking at least one prescription medication long-term (in tablet or capsule form)
• Ability to provide meaningful self-reports (as assessed by the treating physicians and the study director conducting the interviews)
• Consent to audio recording of the individual interview

Inclusion criteria for individual interviews with relatives of older adults or geriatric patients:
• Fully consenting, community-dwelling relatives of older adults or geriatric patients
• Relatives of older adults or geriatric patients who are currently taking at least one prescription medication long-term
• Consent to audio recording of the individual interview

Inclusion criteria for focus group interviews with healthcare professionals in the geriatric sector:
• Professional contact with older adults (over 65 years) or geriatric patients (physicians, nursing staff, pharmacists, emergency services)
• Consent to audio recording of the focus group interview
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for individual interviews with older adults or geriatric patients:
• Older adults OR geriatric patients diagnosed with dementia, delirium, or any other condition that impairs the ability to provide informed consent
• Currently taking fewer than one prescription medication long-term (in tablet or capsule form) 
• Refusal to consent to audio recording of the individual interview

Exclusion criteria for individual interviews with relatives of older adults or geriatric patients:
• Relatives with impaired ability to provide informed consent
• Relatives in inpatient medical treatment or long-term residential care
• Relatives of older adults or geriatric patients who are currently taking fewer than one prescription medication long-term (in tablet or capsule form)
• Refusal to consent to audio recording of the individual interview

Exclusion criteria for focus group interviews with healthcare professionals in the geriatric sector:
• No professional contact with older adults (over 65 years) or geriatric patients in the last 10 years
• Refusal to consent to audio recording of the focus group interview
